product_question: What does Local Law 119 actually require, and which reporting duties are observable on the public surface?

law_custody.publisher: New York City Council and Office of the City Clerk

taxlane_assessment.reason: The enacted law requires citywide reports disaggregated by borough, not community district or division. Website, citywide/borough, and 147-month public-model surfaces are observed, but Council/Mayor submission and a discrete yearly report are not verified. Full compliance, pass/fail, and fiscal claims remain held.

next_evidence.reporting: Capture Council/Mayor submission receipts and a discrete yearly report if publicly available.
next_evidence.outcomes: Join privacy-safe patient outcomes and population exposure at a compatible definition and time basis.
next_evidence.operations: Test demand, call processing, staffing, fleet, posting, routing, and hospital-interface drivers.
next_evidence.candidate: Only then bound one intervention with effect, cost, incidence, delivery, and do-no-harm evidence.

role_review.corrected_claim: Section 15-129 requires borough, not community-district or division, disaggregation.
deferred_claims: outcomes, causality, adequacy, intervention, savings, allocation, and rates

public_warning: Local Law 119 requires monthly and yearly reports to the Council and Mayor, website posting, citywide results, and borough disaggregation. It does not require community-district or division reporting. The public website and 147-month semantic-model history are observable, but formal submission and a discrete yearly report were not verified; no full-compliance, performance, fiscal, allocation, or rate claim follows.
